display_name: Send peer message by role name
description: Resolve a role name (Coordinator, Architect, Git-Controller, etc.) via the agent_role_binding state table (resolve_role_binding) and dispatch a peer_send to whichever session currently holds that role. Eliminates the staleness footgun of addressing by agent_instance_id: scheduled wake-ups, dispatch briefs, and coordinator replies can reference durable names instead of ephemeral bridge UUIDs. Resolution happens at SEND TIME — the current routing tuple is picked up automatically if the binding was refreshed or re-claimed (via peer_claim_role / the /rename skill). v10 Control #4 makes the dispatch persist-first: the envelope is written durably BEFORE delivery, so an offline/unreachable holder yields delivery='queued_for_replay' (durable, delivered=false; the Control #5 repair drain re-delivers on the holder's reattach/reclaim) instead of a hard failure. IMPORTANT-marker behavior (prepend 'IMPORTANT: ' to trigger a native wake) and persisted_silent (no marker, surface via peer_inbox) work unchanged. A role with no binding at all is rejected with peer_role_vacant BEFORE any persist (Scope-decision C).
embedding_description: Send a peer message addressed by durable role name - Coordinator, Architect, Git-Controller - rather than by an ephemeral session id, resolving the name to its current holder at send time. Survives reconnects, so it suits scheduled wake-ups, coordinator dispatch, and watchdog pings. An offline holder has it queued for durable replay.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Peer message delivered by role name
result_processor_customizations.result_description: thread_id, message_id, delivery channel (persisted_silent / queued_notification / queued_wake / queued_watcher / queued_for_replay), plus the resolved (resolved_agent_id, resolved_agent_instance_id, resolved_session_label) the name pointed at when the call was made. A queued_notification / queued_wake channel means the event was placed on the holder's live bridge queue, not that a turn started (REL-06 honest naming). delivery='queued_watcher' means the holder is a no-MCP watch subprocess: the message streams into its watch output and the session sees it when it next looks — pull delivery, never a live interrupt. delivery='queued_for_replay' means the binding resolved but the holder was unreachable, so the envelope is durably persisted (delivered=false) and the repair drain re-delivers it.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the message reached (or was durably queued for) the named role; surface delivery channel + resolved_session_label so the caller knows which concrete session was targeted. queued_for_replay is a SUCCESS (no loss), not a failure; queued_watcher is a SUCCESS delivered pull-style (the holder acts on it at its next look — do not expect an immediate reply turn).

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Resolves a role name via the agent_role_binding state table (resolve_role_binding) and dispatches a persist-first peer_send to the currently-bound (agent_id, agent_instance_id) pair.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: peer_role_vacant: no agent_role_binding row exists for the given name — either it was never claimed or it was released (rejected BEFORE any persist, Scope-decision C). peer_role_malformed: the binding exists but is missing agent_instance_id (corrupted state; re-claim via peer_claim_role). bridge.not_running: start_interface has not been called yet. state_service_unavailable: the state_service is not bound on this homunculus. (An offline holder is NOT an error — it returns delivery='queued_for_replay'.)
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: peer_role_vacant: have the intended role-holder run peer_claim_role with their (agent_id, agent_instance_id). peer_role_malformed: same — re-claim from the role-holder's session. bridge.not_running: wait for start_interface to complete. state_service_unavailable: bind the state_service (postgres_state_management_plugin) in service_bindings.json.
